title: Book Two · Chapter 115: At the Gate Again
story:
Ronan sets a small table near the school gate on Wednesday. Miss Wu has asked the school. He can use the space during lunch. A clean notice stands against a brick.

GUIDE CORRECTIONS.

He has a pencil, two paper strips, and the new back pages. He also has the list with seven empty squares.

A girl arrives first with her folder. Her guide has soft corners.

“My brother used it,” she says.

“Did he go to the room?”

“No. He asked me first.”

Ronan corrects her page. He gives her a separate notice for her brother.

“Thursday after lunch this term,” he says.

She reads it back. He marks one square.

Next comes the boy from the first day. His bag is no longer empty. It holds a school book and a small lunch box.

“I went last Thursday,” he says. “I got my book then.”

“Good.”

“My sister came back to the gate twice on Wednesday.”

Ronan stops with his pencil above the page.

“I am sorry. I gave you the wrong time.”

“She says you must tell people sooner.”

“Yes.”

He does not add that the teacher was busy. He does not mention the rain. He gives the boy the corrected page. He waits while the boy reads it.

The boy stops at this term.

“My sister keeps these days for me.”

“Please show her this part too.”

Ronan puts a finger below the complete line. He does not cover the room name with his hand.

The boy reads from the day to the end once more. Then he puts the guide in his bag, away from his lunch box.

Ronan leaves the pencil on the table until the boy has closed the bag. He wants to hurry to the next empty square. The person in front of him still needs time for the new words.

At the end of the table, the clean back pages move in the wind. He puts his notebook across their corners.

The boy lifts one hand as he leaves. Ronan lifts his own, then turns back to the list.

He has changed a line and spoken to one pupil. There are still places he cannot reach from this little table.

Jun passes the gate with two classmates. He sees the table. One classmate slows down, but Jun keeps walking. Ronan looks at his list again.

By the end of lunch, he has four new marks. Three copies remain. One is at another family's home. Two still have no name.

Miss Wu comes to take the table back.

“I cannot find the last two,” Ronan says.

“We can leave the notice up. Other teachers have the correction. You will keep asking when you see a guide.”

“Will all eighteen come back?”

“Perhaps not.”

Ronan looks through his stack. A wrong page can stay in a bag or under a bed. He cannot reach every place at once.

They carry the table indoors. He puts the corrected copies in a clearly marked box. The old desk copies go in a different place for the teacher.

At the end of the day, a small girl runs to the reading room door. She holds a guide in both hands.

“Is this where I bring it?”

“Yes.”

Ronan takes out his pencil again. The girl watches his whole correction. Then she points to Mei's picture.

“This part helped me find you.”

Ronan looks at the two doors in the picture.

“Mei drew that,” he says.

He gives the guide back to the girl. Mei's picture is clear. The right day is on the back.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

correction＝更正；separate＝单独的；stack＝一叠；sooner＝更早。

## 理解问题

1. 新生姐姐因错误时间多走了几次？
2. Ronan怎样保留Mei实际贡献的署名？

## 读句子

**He / marks / one square.** 他／标记／一个方格。
